'''Flamengo MDL''' is a Brazilian team, the esports division of traditional sports team '''CR Flamengo'''. They are currently known as '''Flamengo Redragon''' for sponsorship reasons.

They initially competed in CBLOL under the management of [[Simplicity Esports]]. Following the partial CBLOL's spot franchise acquisition by '''Los Grandes''' in 2022 they had to rename to [[Flamengo Los Grandes]] due to Riot rules and aftermost with the full acquisition to [[Los Grandes]].

'''Flamengo Esports''' returned to the scene in late 2023 with a new management company, '''Medellin''', which also manages other rosters in the team, including Free Fire and CS2.

== History ==
'''Flamengo Esports''' team was created on late 2017 as a branch of the traditional football club '''CR Flamengo'''. Initial roster included [[Jisu]], [[SirT]], [[Evrot]], [[BrTT]] and [[EsA]], and made its first appearance on [[BRCC 2018 Split 1]]. As runner-ups, they classified for the [[CBLOL/2018 Season/Split 2 Promotion and Access|Access Series]] and made it to brazil's first division by winning over [[Team oNe eSports]]. The Esports team inherited lots of supporters from its football club, and its initial investment was frequently recognized by [[CBLOL]]'s casters as a big step up for Esports in Brazil.

During 2020 and until the merge with [[Los Grandes]], '''Flamengo Esports''' operations were managed by [[Simplicity Esports]].

Flamengo Esports returned to the competitive League scene in October 2023 to play the Multiplatform eSports Games (MEG) League Championship after a rebranding and a new management company managing the team's operations, Medellin, with a roster of old players from the Brazilian scene and from the [[CBLOL/2019 Season/Split 2|CBLOL 2019 2nd Split]] winning team, including [[Goku]] and [[Absolut]]. <ref>https://twitter.com/flaesports/status/1716231744272163267 Flamengo Esports Tweet</ref>

Flamengo players and supporters often refer to themselves as "nação rubro-negra" (red-and-black nation).
